statements.impact_statement: The Marvin timing sidechannel leaks information about an RSA PRIVATE key through the timing of private-key operations, so what matters is whether a FerroEHR process performs one. Two paths reach the crate. Through `openidconnect`, in the OIDC authentication path, the sole RSA operation is verifying an RS256 signature on an ID token with the identity provider's PUBLIC key: there is no secret in that computation for a timing observation to recover. Through `pgp`, in VERSION signing, an RSA operation would be a private-key one — but only in `[signing] mode = "pgp"`, which is not the default: the shipped default is `digest` mode (SHA-256 over the canonical form), which uses no asymmetric key at all, so the default artifact performs no RSA private-key operation. A deployment that does enable `pgp` mode chooses its own OpenPGP key, and an ECC/EdDSA signing key keeps `rsa` off the signing path entirely; a deployment that enables `pgp` mode with an RSA key is outside this statement and should rotate to an ECC key. `ferroehr-ext` reaches the crate through the same two carriers as the platform library it extends, so the same argument covers it. The viewer (`ferroehr-viewer`) reaches the crate through `openidconnect` alone, in its OIDC login, where the only RSA operation is the same PUBLIC-key verification of the identity provider's ID-token signature; it does not depend on `pgp`. The spec crates (`openehr-rm`, `openehr-its`, `openehr-sdt`, `openehr-adl`) reach `rsa` only through their path-only dev-dependency on the `testkit` harness (which depends on the platform library): a test-only edge cargo strips at packaging, so no published crate ships the code at all. No upstream fix exists — `rsa` has no patched release — so this is not a deferred upgrade. Re-evaluate if a release beyond rsa 0.9 ships, or if the default signing mode changes.

The advisory concerns crypto-bigint operations meant to be constant-time (borrowing subtraction, trailing-zero counting, `div_rem`, `nlimbs`, Montgomery multiplication, `UintRef` equality) that can branch on their operands, which leaks only when an operand is SECRET. crypto-bigint 0.5.5 is reached through `cx448` (Ed448) and `elliptic-curve` 0.13 (the ECDSA curves `p256`, `p384`, `p521`, `k256`), all carried by `pgp`, and through `p256` and `p384` under `openidconnect`. In VERSION signing (`[signing] mode = "pgp"`, not the default `digest` mode), an ECDSA or Ed448 signature would run that arithmetic over the private key and the nonce, so `PgpKey::from_parts` in `app/ferroehr/src/versioning/signature/key.rs` refuses either algorithm as the signing component with `KeyError::RefusedAlgorithm` before the boot check makes any signature, and the server does not start (#3965). Ed25519 signs on `curve25519-dalek` and RSA on `num-bigint-dig`, neither of which reaches the crate. What remains is verification: of VERSION signatures against the configured and retired certificates, of the licence token against the licensor's certificates, and, in the viewer, of the identity provider's ES256 or ES384 ID-token signature. Every operand there is a public key, a public signature or a public digest, so a timing observation has no secret to recover. Parsing an unencrypted ECDSA secret key file checks the scalar's range once before the refusal; that runs at boot over an operator's local file and cannot be repeated or timed by an adversary. The spec crates reach the crate only through their path-only dev-dependency on `testkit`, which cargo strips at packaging. No fix exists on the 0.5 line (only 0.7.6 and later are patched), and no release of `pgp` (0.21.0), `cx448` (0.1.1) or `openidconnect` (4.0.1) leaves it. Re-evaluate when `pgp` and `openidconnect` release on crypto-bigint 0.7.6 or later, and before the signing refusal is lifted.
